Democrats Lead in Alaska and Mississippi Senate Races as House Majority Approaches 260 Seats
Nov 06, 2026
Link copied
Democrats continue to build on their historic gains in Tuesday’s midterm elections as final results are tabulated. So far, Democrats have won 253 House seats compared to Republicans’ 157, with 25 races still undecided.
In Mississippi, Democrat Scott Colom has added to his narrow lead over incumbent Republican Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith. He’s currently ahead by more than 1,800 votes as election officials process provisional ballots and late-arriving mail ballots. Colom would be the first Black senator from Mississippi since Blanche K. Bruce was elected in 1875, during the Reconstruction era.
In Alaska, Democrat Mary Peltola narrowly leads incumbent Republican Senator Dan Sullivan by just over 600 votes, though a quarter of ballots remain to be counted. If Democrats win Alaska and Mississippi, their Senate caucus will grow to 56 members.

Incoming Freshman Senators Call for New Leadership to Replace Top Democrat Chuck Schumer
Nov 06, 2026
Link copied
There are growing calls for new leadership to challenge Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer and House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries. Senators-elect Peggy Flanagan, Troy Jackson, Abdul El-Sayed, Juliana Stratton and Adam Hamilton have all said they won’t support Schumer, as has Senate candidate Scott Colom in Mississippi. This is Michigan Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed speaking with The Bulwark after Tuesday’s election.
Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed: “I’ve had conversations, obviously, with Senator Schumer in the context of this race. I’ve been clear: I want new leadership, and I want leadership that is focused on getting money out of politics, putting money in your pocket, passing Medicare for All. But at the end of the day, it’s a choice between two or more options, so I want to see who else is willing to put their hat in the ring.”
On Wednesday, CNN’s Manu Raju asked Senator Schumer about growing calls for him to step down as Senate Democratic leader.
Manu Raju: “How do you deal with those candidates who won who say they’re not going to vote for you?”
Sen. Chuck Schumer: “Look” —
Manu Raju: “Adam Hamilton, Troy Jackson, Abdul El-Sayed?”
Sen. Chuck Schumer: “OK, again, to repeat the answer: The issue is not me. I’ll be reelected as majority leader.”
In Texas, Senator-elect James Talarico has refused to commit to backing Schumer. Talarico is also calling on fellow Democrats to abolish the filibuster, a rule that effectively requires 60 of the Senate’s 100 members to pass legislation. Talarico spoke with NBC News.
Sen.-elect James Talarico: “I believe that the majority has the right to govern in this country. And the filibuster, which is not in the Constitution — it’s a Jim Crow relic — it is — it is leading to gridlock.”
Meanwhile, an online petition calling on Democrats to reject New York Congressmember Hakeem Jeffries as House speaker in the new Congress has garnered over 830,000 signatures.

Pete Hegseth Defends Iran War, Demands $350B in Additional Funding and Vows to Fight Impeachment
Nov 06, 2026
Link copied
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth defended the Iran war and lashed out at his critics on Thursday, as the House of Representatives prepares to vote as early as next week on articles of impeachment. The effort to oust Hegseth is being led by Kentucky’s outgoing Republican Congressmember Thomas Massie, who gave Hegseth an ultimatum after Tuesday’s historic losses for Republicans: Resign or be removed by Congress. The effort appears to have enough bipartisan support to pass, after many Republican lawmakers turned on Hegseth following their party’s election rout. On Thursday, Hegseth posted a defiant video on social media in which he lavished praise on President Trump, demanded at least $350 billion in additional military funding, said transgender troops have a mental illness incompatible with military service, and claimed victory over diversity, equity and inclusion, which he called a “Marxist ideology built to destroy us.” And Hegseth vowed to fight against impeachment.
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth: “It’s all about the politics of personal destruction. Didn’t work against President Trump, and it won’t work with me.”

Harmeet Dhillon Resigns as Head of DOJ’s Civil Rights Division
Nov 06, 2026
Link copied
Harmeet Dhillon has resigned from her post as chief of the Justice Department’s Civil Rights Division. Dhillon is the first top official to leave the Trump administration following the Republicans’ crushing defeat in the midterm elections. Ahead of the midterms, Dhillon was part of Trump’s unsuccessful crusade to force states to turn over sensitive voting data. Dhillon spent her 19-month tenure gutting civil rights, and diversity, equity and inclusion protections in education, and led the campaign to target dozens of universities nationwide over student-led pro-Palestine activism and campus protests. Under Dhillon, the DOJ’s Civil Rights Division stopped investigating accusations of systemic racism and sexism, and in January refused to probe the fatal shootings of Renee Good and Alex Pretti by federal immigration agents in Minneapolis. Dhillon overhauled the Civil Rights Division from its original purpose of fighting discrimination and Jim Crow-era injustices to prosecute the left and other dissent.

DSA Candidates Win Mayor’s Races in L.A., D.C., Ann Arbor and Providence
Nov 06, 2026
Link copied
At least four members of the Democratic Socialists of America have won mayor’s races in major U.S. cities, following Zohran Mamdani’s successful campaign for New York City mayor one year ago. In Los Angeles, Nithya Raman has defeated incumbent Mayor Karen Bass. Raman shared this video message yesterday.
Mayor-elect Nithya Raman: “And that work starts now, so that we can build housing that people can afford, parks for our children to play in, a transit system that can get people where they need to go, a city that is safe for its working people and its families, and a city government that is actually capable of delivering on its promises.”
Democratic socialist Janeese Lewis George has been elected mayor of Washington, D.C., and becomes D.C.’s first new mayor since 2015, after incumbent Muriel Bowser did not seek reelection.
Providence, Rhode Island, elected democratic socialist David Morales as mayor. At 28 years old, he is also the youngest mayor in Providence’s history. Morales has vowed to fight for working people and immigrants.
And DSA candidate Yousef Rabhi has claimed victory in the mayoral race in Ann Arbor, Michigan. Rabhi campaigned on building more city-subsidized affordable housing, labor rights and proposing a moratorium on data centers.

Democratic Socialist Angela Gonzales-Torres Beats AIPAC-Backed Democrat for L.A. House Seat
Nov 06, 2026
Link copied
A record number of candidates backed by the Democratic Socialists of America have won U.S. House seats. The latest victory comes in California’s 34th Congressional District, where DSA member Angela Gonzales-Torres has unseated Democratic incumbent Jimmy Gomez to represent parts of Los Angeles. Gomez faced a House ethics probe over sexual assault allegations from a former staffer. He also had the support of AIPAC, the American Israel Public Affairs Committee, which spent more than $2.6 million on Gomez’s political campaigns.
Angela Gonzales-Torres was born in the neighborhood of Highland Park. Her father, an auto mechanic, was deported to Mexico when she was just 15 years old. She will represent one of the poorest districts in the United States. So far, at least six DSA-backed freshman Congressmembers are headed to the House, joining Reps. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Rashida Tlaib.

Lawrence is co-founder of the Sunrise Movement and centered his campaign on opposition to data centers and Flock camera surveillance. He’s also proposed tighter AI restrictions. Lawrence will represent Michigan’s 7th Congressional District, which includes Lansing.

Gov. Gavin Newsom Commutes Death Sentences of All Death Row Prisoners
Nov 06, 2026
Link copied
In California, outgoing Democratic Governor Gavin Newsom announced Thursday he will grant clemency to all prisoners currently on death row. They now face life in prison without the possibility of parole. Newsom’s move came seven years after he placed a moratorium on executions in California. In a statement, Nadia Daar, executive director of Amnesty International USA, said, “California has gone two decades without an execution, yet, with more than 550 people, has the largest death row in the nation. Governor Newsom’s decision turns that long pause into meaningful and lasting progress against an inherently cruel, discriminatory and irreversible system that is antithetical to human rights.”

U.S. Held Secret Talks with Tehran in Bid to Deport Iranians, Despite “Threat of Certain Death”
Nov 06, 2026
Link copied
Newly published court transcripts have revealed the Trump administration is knowingly deporting people detained in the U.S. to Iran — despite ongoing U.S. attacks. Trump officials have reportedly been holding secret talks with Tehran to coordinate the removals, including of Iranians who fear torture and persecution if they’re returned to Iran. Court documents unsealed on Thursday show U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes appeared incredulous as a Justice Department lawyer revealed the plans. Judge Reyes asked, “What you’re telling me is that the United States of America is going to send individuals back to that region facing what you and I and everyone who would ever look at this would know would be at a minimum a serious threat of certain death?” The government lawyer responded, “Yes, Your Honor.”

Over 600,000 March in France as Unions Hold Strike to Protest Austerity and Rising Prices
Nov 06, 2026
Link copied
In France, hundreds of thousands of workers walked off their jobs Thursday and marched in nearly 200 cities in a one-day nationwide strike to demand higher wages and funding for education and other public services. Most of the unions participating were in France’s public sector. The demonstrations follow weeks of protests led by high school students demanding an end to chronic teacher shortages, overcrowded classrooms and crumbling school buildings. This is the mother of a student protester who joined a march in Paris.
Julie Souman: “As the parent of a student, we have mobilized to protect our children, because we have seen the images, like everyone else, of police violence on the TV and what has been reported at other Paris high schools, particularly at Hélène Boucher and Ravel. And since we don’t want this to get out of hand, we are here to ensure their protection, quite simply.”

Paraguay’s Trump-Supported President Resigns, Faces Criminal Probe Following Bank’s Collapse
Nov 06, 2026
Link copied
Paraguayan President Santiago Peña has resigned following the collapse of the major digital lender Ueno Bank, to which Peña had business ties. Ueno’s demise left at least 3 million people — nearly half of Paraguay’s population — without access to their money and froze hundreds of millions of dollars in public funds, including state pension money. Peña, who is a Trump ally, now faces a criminal investigation.

Russell Brand Found Guilty of Rape and Sexual Assaults
Nov 06, 2026
Link copied
In the United Kingdom, the comedian, actor and podcaster Russell Brand has been found guilty of raping a fan and sexually assaulting three other women. The abuses occurred between 2004 and 2009 at the peak of Brand’s career. This is Metropolitan Police Detective Superintendent Andy Furphy speaking outside a London courthouse following the jury’s guilty verdicts.
Andy Furphy: “Russell Brand used his influence, status and fame to prey on and exploit women. As his profile grew, so, too, did his sense of entitlement. Today’s verdict sends a clear message that no one is above the law, regardless of their fame, wealth, influence or public profile.”

Los demócratas lideran las contiendas en Alaska y Misisipi para el Senado de EE.UU. al tiempo que se encaminan a obtener 260 escaños en la Cámara de Representantes
06 Nov. 2026
Link copied
En Estados Unidos, los demócratas siguen consolidando los logros históricos obtenidos en las elecciones de mitad de mandato del martes a medida que se completan los escrutinios. Hasta el momento, los demócratas han obtenido 253 escaños en la Cámara de Representantes, mientras que los republicanos han conseguido 157, al tiempo que aún quedan 25 contiendas por definir. En el estado de Misisipi, el demócrata Scott Colom ha ampliado la estrecha ventaja que mantiene sobre la actual senadora republicana Cindy Hyde-Smith. Colom lleva actualmente una ventaja de más de 1.800 votos al tiempo que los funcionarios electorales continúan contabilizando boletas provisionales y papeletas de voto por correo que llegaron una vez finalizadas las votaciones del martes. De resultar ganador, Colom se convertiría en el primer senador negro por Misisipi desde que Blanche K. Bruce fue elegido en 1875, durante el período de la Reconstrucción que siguió a la guerra civil estadounidense. En el estado de Alaska, la demócrata Mary Peltola aventaja por un estrecho margen de poco más de 600 votos al actual senador republicano Dan Sullivan, aunque todavía queda por escrutar una cuarta parte de las papeletas. Si los demócratas ganan en Alaska y Misisipi, pasarán a tener 56 miembros en el Senado de Estados Unidos.

Senadores demócratas electos piden un nuevo liderazgo para reemplazar al líder demócrata del Senado de EE.UU., Chuck Schumer
06 Nov. 2026
Link copied
Cada vez son más las voces que reclaman un nuevo liderazgo que dispute el puesto al líder del bloque demócrata en el Senado estadounidense, Chuck Schumer, y al líder demócrata en la Cámara de Representantes, Hakeem Jeffries. Los senadores electos Peggy Flanagan, Troy Jackson, Abdul El-Sayed, Juliana Stratton y Adam Hamilton, así como el candidato al Senado por Misisipi Scott Colom, han manifestado que no apoyarán a Schumer. Estas fueron las palabras expresadas por el senador electo de Michigan Abdul El-Sayed en declaraciones que brindó al medio The Bulwark tras las elecciones del martes.
Senador electo Abdul El-Sayed: “Obviamente he mantenido conversaciones con el senador Schumer en el contexto de esta contienda. He dejado claro que quiero un nuevo liderazgo, que se enfoque en acabar con la influencia del dinero en la política, aumentar el dinero disponible en los bolsillos de la gente y aprobar el 'Medicare para todos'. Pero, en definitiva, se trata de elegir entre dos o más opciones, así que quiero ver quién más está dispuesto a postularse”.
El “Medicare para todos” es una propuesta que busca ampliar a toda la población estadounidense la disponibilidad del programa público de salud Medicare.
El miércoles, el periodista de la cadena de noticias CNN Manu Raju le preguntó al senador Schumer sobre los crecientes pedidos para que dimita como líder del bloque demócrata del Senado.
Manu Raju: “¿Qué les responde a esos candidatos que ganaron [las elecciones] y que dicen que no van a votar por usted?”.
Senador Chuck Schumer: “Mire…”.
Manu Raju: “¿[Qué les responde a] Adam Hamilton, Troy Jackson, Abdul El-Sayed?”.
Senador Chuck Schumer: “Bien, repito la respuesta: yo no soy el problema. Seré reelegido como líder de la mayoría [en el Senado]”.
En el estado de Texas, el senador electo James Talarico se ha negado a comprometerse a respaldar a Schumer. Talarico también está instando a sus colegas demócratas a eliminar el obstruccionismo legislativo, una regla que, en la práctica, obliga a obtener el respaldo de 60 de los 100 senadores para aprobar una legislación. Estas fueron las palabras expresadas por Talarico en declaraciones a la cadena NBC News.
Senador electo James Talarico: “Creo que la mayoría tiene derecho a gobernar en este país. Y el obstruccionismo, que no figura en la Constitución y es un vestigio de [las leyes segregacionistas de época del] Jim Crow, está provocando un estancamiento legislativo”.
Mientras tanto, una petición en internet que insta a los demócratas a rechazar al congresista de Nueva York Hakeem Jeffries como presidente de la Cámara de Representantes en el próximo Congreso estadounidense ya ha reunido más de 830.000 firmas.

Pete Hegseth defiende la guerra contra Irán, exige 350.000 millones de dólares adicionales para el presupuesto militar y promete luchar contra el juicio político en su contra
06 Nov. 2026
Link copied
El secretario de Defensa de Estados Unidos, Pete Hegseth, defendió el jueves la guerra contra Irán y arremetió contra sus críticos, al tiempo que la Cámara de Representantes se prepara para votar, la próxima semana, sobre los artículos para iniciar un juicio político en su contra. La iniciativa para destituir a Hegseth está liderada por el congresista republicano saliente del estado de Kentucky Thomas Massie, quien, tras las históricas derrotas de los republicanos en las elecciones del martes, le lanzó un ultimátum: o renuncia o será destituido por el Congreso. La iniciativa parece contar con suficiente apoyo bipartidista para ser aprobada, después de que numerosos legisladores republicanos le dieran la espalda a Hegseth tras el contundente revés electoral de su partido. Mississippi’s race for the U.S. Senate remains too close to call: Democrat Scott Colom is narrowly leading Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith by nearly 2,000 votes with 96% of votes counted as of Friday morning. Donald Trump carried Mississippi by 23 points in 2024. If elected, Colom would be the first Democrat to win the state in 40 years and the first African American since 1875, during the Reconstruction era. Colom, the former district attorney for northeast Mississippi, made the issue of affordability central to his campaign. He has sharply criticized national Democrats for writing off Mississippi and failing to invest in his campaign early on.
“The entire country shifted left. But when you look at it regionally, the biggest shifts took place in the South — Texas, Mississippi, South Carolina, Louisiana,” says Cliff Albright, executive director of Black Voters Matter. That “wave of energy” was “largely led by Black voters who were most under attack with the mid-decade racial gerrymandering that was taking place. It clearly backfired, and all it did was to wake up a sleeping giant.”
“Without the extreme gerrymandering, without the extreme voter restrictions that have been seen throughout the South, [the] wave would have been even bigger,” adds Chris Kromm, executive director of the Institute for Southern Studies. “There’s a real opportunity for engaging more voters and really pushing the region in a more progressive direction.”

Transcript
This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form.
AMY GOODMAN: We begin today’s show in the Deep South, where Mississippi’s Senate race remains too close to call. Democrat Scott Colom is narrowly leading Republican incumbent Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith by more than 1,800 votes as election officials process provisional ballots and late-arriving mail ballots. Just two years ago, Donald Trump carried Mississippi by 23 points. If elected, Scott Colom would be the first Democrat to win the state in 40 years and the first African American since 1875, during Reconstruction.
Colom made the issue of affordability central to his campaign, and in an ad that went viral, he blasted Senator Hyde-Smith for saying Mississippians should, quote, “pick another protein,” unquote, if they’re upset over high beef prices. The ad features Mississippians saying they’d rather pick another senator.
HUGH KEETON: The price of beef continuing to go up.
SEN. CINDY HYDE-SMITH: You know, you have so many proteins to choose from.
MISSISSIPPI VOTER 1: Pick another protein? [bleep], I’d rather pick another senator instead.
MISSISSIPPI VOTER 2: Pick another protein? She done lost her damn mind. I’d rather pick another senator.
MISSISSIPPI VOTER 3: Pick another protein? What the [bleep]?
SCOTT COLOM: Pick another senator instead.
AMY GOODMAN: Scott Colom is a former district attorney for northeast Mississippi. In 2022, President Biden nominated him to the federal bench, a nomination blocked by Colom’s opponent in this race, incumbent Republican Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith.
Colom has sharply criticized national Democrats for writing off Mississippi and failing to invest in his campaign. Early on, he told reporters, quote, “Mississippi was never a lost cause. We were a betrayed cause.” This is Colom speaking to NBC News.
SCOTT COLOM: The reality is our country does not do well when it ignores places like Mississippi. … You can’t lead with doubt. You have to believe. You have to lead with belief, and that’s where the power is. When you believe things, you can actually achieve it. And there’s some people in the party that they are just treading water. Right? “What’s the path to least resistance to get to 51? Oh my gosh, we did it.” That’s not the right way to think. In this particular moment, you have to think about how can we win everywhere, because we need to represent working people in a way where we actually deliver.

Vanity Fair recently published an excerpt from longtime investigative reporter Matthew Cole’s new book, Princes and Thieves: Jared Kushner and Mohamed bin Zayed’s Secret Plot to Remake the Middle East.
The excerpt alleged that during President Trump’s first term, Saudi and Emirati leaders secretly put at least $2 billion into bank accounts and gave access to Kushner. At the time, Jared Kushner was serving as senior adviser to President Trump, his father-in-law. He is now Trump’s special envoy. Kushner’s lawyers responded by demanding that Vanity Fair retract the article and threatening legal action against the book publisher, Simon & Schuster.
Jared Kushner denied the report, saying, “The allegations made by this author are completely insane, categorically false, and never happened. We denied every one of these claims on the record, yet the author failed to provide a single shred of evidence to substantiate any of them.” His lawyers say no such bank accounts existed and that the allegations are unsupported by the verifiable evidence.
In an extended interview with Democracy Now!, author Matthew Cole stood by his reporting. “This book is a result of more than 50 sources. There was an enormous amount of fact-checking and legal vetting that went into this book,” says Cole. “There’s plenty of information and reporting in the book that lets us establish and understand that there was … an unholy alliance between Jared Kushner and the leader of the UAE, the leader of Saudi Arabia and, at the time, Benjamin Netanyahu, the prime minister of Israel.”
On Friday, Congressmember Jamie Raskin, the ranking Democrat on the House Judiciary Committee, called on Kushner to recuse himself from Middle East and Ukraine negotiations and to produce a “comprehensive list of bank accounts or other financial instruments” that he had access to during his time in government.
